newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Sept 26.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:
* Israeli and Palenstinian forces exchanged gunfire in the West Bank, leaving five Arabs dead and hundreds wounded.
* Empire Blue Cross and Blue Shield said it would seek New York State approval to convert itself into a for-profit company.
* Renowned heart surgeon Dr Michael DeBakey, after meeting with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, said Yeltsin was in better condition than first thought.
* Boris Yeltsin's surgical team said the Russian president would go ahead with heart surgery and was expected to make a full recovery.
* Reform Party presidential nominee Ross Perot has found a sharper focus for his 1996 campaign by not so much running for president as running against Washington political institutions.
* An Islamic fundamentalist army vowing to install a strict Moslem government in Afghanistan moved into the capital, Kabul.
* A potential security flaw has been found in electronic cash cards, which are widely used in Europe and being tested in the United States.
